# SEO-228: Serve responsive image candidates sized for the layout

This page is generated from the canonical JSONL registry record. Edit the JSONL record and run `npm run docs -- --write`; do not edit this file directly.

## Statement

An image whose displayed width varies with the viewport offers several candidate sources with their pixel widths declared, together with a description of the space it will occupy, so the browser can choose rather than always fetching the largest file.

## Rationale

A single large asset scaled down in the browser transfers bytes no reader benefits from, and on a narrow connection those bytes delay the content the reader came for.

## Applicability

```json
{
  "all": [
    "public_site"
  ],
  "any": [
    "has_images"
  ]
}
```

## Implementation

Generate the candidate set from the source asset during the build, or use the framework image component that does so, and describe the layout width honestly rather than copying a value from another template. A fixed-size image needs no candidate set.

## Verification

- Level: `SOURCE_AND_RUNTIME`
- Method: Load each page at several viewport widths and record which candidate the browser selected against the width the image actually occupied.
- Evidence: `BROWSER`, `RENDERED_HTML`, `PERFORMANCE_MEASUREMENT`
- Automated check: none.

- Frameworks: `any`
